_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#4, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: pure Newton at Re > ~200 diverges from an at-rest guess, exploding within 2-3 iterations, and 5 Picard steps first bring the state into Newton's basin. Ran: lid-driven cavity, Taylor-Hood, one pressure DOF pinned, always from rest -- Re = 100/200/400 on MeshTri().refined(3); Re = 800 on refined(3) AND refined(4); Re = 800 on refined(4) with 5 Picard steps first; and a continuation ramp through Re = 100/200/400/600/800 on refined(3) starting each solve from the previous solution. Printed: THREE THINGS ARE WRONG. (1) 'Re > ~200 diverges' -- pure Newton from rest converges at Re = 200 AND 400 on refined(3), in 3-4 iterations. (2) Where it does fail (Re = 800, refined(3)) the cause is the MESH, not the Reynolds number: the same Re from the same at-rest guess converges in 5 iterations on refined(4), so the entry reads an under-resolved discretisation as a nonlinear-solver problem. (3) It does not 'explode within 2-3 iterations' -- the residual stagnates within a factor 1.469 for four iterations (3.960e-02 / 4.441e-02 / 5.815e-02 / 5.157e-02) before blowing up, so a watchdog armed for an early explosion sees a plausible plateau. AND THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY MAKES IT WORSE: at Re = 800 on refined(4), where pure Newton converges, 5 Picard steps then Newton DIVERGES. A remedy that does work is continuation in Re, which converges at every step of the ramp including the Re = 800 that fails from rest on the same coarse mesh.
